paper_metadata.title: Quantum Arithmetic for Directly Embedded Arrays

summary: The paper proposes a gate‑based framework for encoding arrays directly into quantum amplitudes and performing arithmetic operations (permutations, reductions, products) on a ‘quantum matrix.’ Generic n‑qubit state preparation is estimated to require ~2^(n+1) CNOT gates, while loading a constant array can be done with n_I X‑gates, two Y‑rotations, and one multi‑controlled NOT. All implementations were tested only in Qiskit with no hardware benchmarks or numerical performance results.

experiments.description: Theoretical gate-based framework for direct embedding of arrays into quantum amplitudes, with example arithmetic operations (reversing, permutations, cyclic shifts, addition/reduction, multiplication by a constant, array multiplication, squaring/scalar product) and information extraction via amplitude estimation/Grover-style amplification. The paper reports implementation and testing in Qiskit, but does not provide a concrete benchmark dataset or hardware run.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Coin (QCoin) / Grover-amplified amplitude extraction within direct-embedding framework

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A two-register quantum matrix |psi> = sum_{i,j} c_ij |i>_nI |j>_nJ with direct embedding of values into amplitudes; auxiliary qubit used for loading and readout. Rows/columns addressed by nI and nJ qubits respectively.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Not a single optimization problem; framework for arithmetic manipulation of arrays and extraction of amplitudes. Example tasks include constant shift f_j -> f_j - s and approximate stepwise linear shift.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Masking with X gates and controlled rotations; post-selection on auxiliary qubit |0>_a or |0>_mul; Grover-style amplification for readout.

problem_instance.description: Generic arrays / quantum matrices; illustrative examples use a 2 x J matrix and then a 4 x J matrix for stepwise linear shift approximation.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uniform superposition loading; pointwise loading of matrix entries or constant-array loading; no real dataset specified.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper states the tools were implemented and tested in Qiskit, but does not report a benchmark protocol, number of runs, or numerical results.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Direct embedding / state preparation angles computed from array values; masking and controlled-rotation construction for loading; Grover-style amplification for amplitude readout.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Empirical estimation of amplitude followed by iterative refinement; extraction of absolute amplitude via QCoin / amplitude estimation.

results.unit: CNOT gates (leading-order scaling for generic n-qubit state preparation)

results.value: exponential refinement via iterative Grover amplification

classical_baselines.method_name: classical loading of a constant array

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic / exponential reduction in loading operations for generic state preparation; exponentially fewer operations for constant-array loading
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical loading of a constant array
speedup_claims.conditions: for loading a constant array into a quantum matrix; generic state preparation still requires efficient oracles and the paper does not prove an end-to-end speedup
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states that generic pointwise loading is not efficient and that overall efficiency depends on the loading oracle. No concrete benchmark or hardware demonstration is reported.

speedup_claims.factor: precision improves from epsilon to epsilon/gamma
speedup_claims.conditions: after Grover-style amplification in the QCoin readout procedure
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a formal relation in the text, not an empirical benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: State preparation for a generic n-qubit state scales as 2^(n+1) CNOTs (leading order) for generic loading; constant-array loading uses nI X-gates, two Y-rotations, and one multi-controlled NOT in the worst case; Grover amplification improves estimation precision iteratively.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical loading of a constant array on a line of the I x J matrix requires J operations; generic classical array handling not characterized asymptotically in the paper.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require efficient oracle-based state preparation and large amplitude-encoded arrays; generic loading currently scales as ~2^(n+1) CNOTs for n-qubit states.
limiting_factors: State preparation cost exponential for generic data (2^(n+1) CNOTs)
No empirical results on real hardware
Efficiency depends on availability of specialized oracles for loading arrays

notes: No concrete hardware device or benchmark run is reported; hardware.type is not specified. Qiskit implementation is explicitly stated, but only as a software framework, not a QPU. The paper gives asymptotic loading complexity and qualitative efficiency discussion, but no end-to-end speedup claim is proven. num_qubits is not fixed because the framework is generic and depends on I, J, and auxiliary registers.
The paper explicitly frames the work as a conceptual framework and toolkit rather than an experimentally benchmarked algorithm.
No numerical experiments, datasets, or hardware runs are reported; therefore any advantage remains theoretical.
